issues.detail: The Hebrew 'מִי יָנוּד לָךְ' means 'who will shake [the head] for you' (i.e., lament/mourn for you), not 'who can comfort you' (which would be 'מִי יְנַחֵם'). The Chinese renders it as '誰能安慰你呢' (who can comfort you), which changes the meaning from mourning/lamenting to comforting. The second clause 'מִי אֲנַחֲמֵךְ' is correctly 'who can comfort you', but the first is mistranslated.
